penalties_applied.name: regulated_industry
penalties_applied.reason: Legal compliance and copyright determination touch IP law; enterprises will demand licensed legal opinions, not just AI-generated flags — this creates a quasi-legal-services dynamic that carries regulatory and liability risk.

rationale: The buyer is real — engineering leads and legal/compliance teams at software companies with existing enterprise tooling budgets — and the copyright exposure problem is genuine and growing. However, the legal dimension is the killer: any tool that flags or classifies code as 'AI-generated' and asserts copyright status is making a quasi-legal claim, which exposes the operator to liability and places it in regulated territory. Additionally, buildability is moderate at best — the scanning and provenance-tracking infrastructure (AST parsing, git-hook integration, CI pipeline connectors) goes well beyond Claude prompts and a Stripe link, requiring meaningful integration work. The total after the regulated-industry penalty drops to 4.1, which is below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: This is not viable for a solo non-technical operator at this stage. The core product would need to integrate with GitHub/GitLab via webhooks, parse code commits to tag AI-generated segments, store provenance records, and produce audit-ready reports — none of which is achievable with Claude + a landing page alone. More critically, any 'AI copyright compliance' claim carries legal liability that would require counsel to stand behind, making this fundamentally a legal-services-adjacent product. A solo operator without legal backing and engineering resources should not attempt this.
notes: Fails regulated_industry threshold. Also misses buildability_with_ai floor (5 < 6) and operational_autonomy floor (6 < 7), so even without the penalty it would be capped at validate. Drop recommended until market is clearer and tooling options mature.
